title: Root cut laws for two-chain words: hub, rectangle and cut bounds (no new κ)
body:
## Result

No new κ and no word. The package `research/p104-root-cut-laws` is a proof note on cut and hub laws for the two-chain roots of the P104 caller. Statements, proofs and a hypothesis ledger are in `THEOREM.md`.

1. **Rectangle law, packing, Theorem S [proved, checked].** For 2 x 2 gains and an odd sign quadruple the four residual ranks sum to at least 2 (three exact cells force the fourth to be 2sI). 72 odd rectangles cover 288 distinct cells of the 18 x 18 grid with no shared cell, so for any two hub coordinates the residual rank over all stage pairs is at least 144. Checked on the two root instances over all 703 and 780 hub pairs: 144 is attained at one pair each.
2. **Theorem H and H' [proved under hypothesis R, one author].** R is the hub rank law quoted from #6881, itself conditional on its grammar. At least ρ coordinates lie in every pivot mask between two pivots. For any label j in the hull, at least rank Z_UU(j) of those coordinates lie in M_j (H'); the proof uses a rank step at E_j = 0. The stronger statement "every mask of the hull" is false: on the t = 0 direct sum of two chain roots, with a rank-1 label at J = 4 or 7 on chain A and the last label on chain B, hub 20 is in every pivot mask and absent from M_J (exact, contract verified). **Scope:** that base root is reducible. Nothing is claimed for connected roots, and nothing about κ.
3. **Root cut [arithmetic proved; law conditional].** Cut per chain = 8[f(18) + 2f(9)] + 87.353 = 819.967, f(x) = x ln x, from the incidences of the two all-pivot roots. It applies to all-pivot words only: words with a t = -1 label have a different incidence multiset. The cost expression is a convention fixed in the note (not verbatim in any cited PR), not derived.
4. **Theorem C [proved, checked].** For flat words and any frame set U: rank T[D+E, A+D] <= n_down and rank T^-1[A+D, D+E] <= n_up - |C| + |D|, and, for T invertible with T = I_D + T'', a cut demand (f, r) costs at least f + r crossings with owned registers and at least 2·max(f, r) without. A non-flat toy shows the flat bound fails; n_down + a_down is proved.

## Review status

Written by one model session; a second model session read the statements and proofs once. No human has reviewed them. Proved by hand and also checked: items 1, 2 (H, H'), the identity in 3, and item 4. Computed only: the data facts, the counterexample and the toy. The hub rank law (hypothesis R, from #6881) and the cost expression are quoted.

## Checks

`python3.12 -I -B research/p104-root-cut-laws/check.py` (a few seconds, standard library only; ends with `PASS_P104_ROOT_CUT_LAWS`): hypotheses and bounds on both roots, all hub pairs, the proof ingredients of H and H', random and exhaustive small-field tests, and failing controls (planted bounds, contract-breaking mutations, an even sign quadruple, characteristic 2). The registered-package validator passes on a scratch copy at base 7c49fe32c.

## Credit

The roots (the root of #6889 is inherited from #6883) and the hub rank law come from #6833, #6881, #6889 and #6902 (DreamingOfClouds, all open). The nullity theorem is classical (Gustafson 1984; Fiedler and Markham 1986) and is reproved in the note.

## Not claimed

No bound on κ; nothing priced; no statement about connected roots with an interior t = -1 stage.
